cands.name: Reggie Bellamy
cands.bio: Former District 2 county commissioner (2018-2022) and Port Authority chair (2021). Born in Bradenton; Army veteran (honorable discharge 1993, corporal); business-administration degree from Bethune-Cookman. Longtime Palmetto High basketball coach, middle-school dean and Executive Director of the Palmetto Youth Center. Lost 2022 re-election to Amanda Ballard after the district was redrawn.
cands.local_ties: Fifth-generation Manatee County resident per The Bradenton Times; Palmetto-based youth work. Home address not stated in the sources.

record.text: Won District 2 in 2018 by beating incumbent Charles Smith in the Democratic primary by 185 votes, then won the general election.
Elected Manatee County Port Authority chairman for one year (Dec 2020).

Late Oct / Nov 2020: voted against a motion to reconsider the county's $32.5M purchase of 161 acres (Musgrave family land beside the Lena Road landfill); the motion failed 4-3. The column links the push to reconsider to developer-backed interests (columnist's inference).
Supported redevelopment of the urban core (downtown Bradenton and Palmetto) and attainable housing (2022 candidate profile).

money_notes.text: Official SOE totals: $25,835 monetary through Oct 29, 2026, including $5,000 from himself; no political-committee gifts other than the county Democratic Executive Committee ($1,500). Almost no real-estate or development occupations in the filings (about $500).
In the 2022 Democratic primary Charles Smith claimed Bellamy took 'almost $100,000' from developers (Smith's claim; not verified).

Bellamy called the claims 'an unfortunate and false statement'. No finding or resignation was found.

m.name: Manatee County Water Quality Protection, Overdevelopment Prevention, Natural Lands Preservation and Public Preserves General Obligation Bonds ($75M, 0.16 mill)
m.summary: Authorizes the county to levy an added 0.16 mill property tax and issue up to $75M in general obligation bonds (20-year maturity, annual audits) to buy, improve and maintain environmental lands and conservation easements (including farmland development rights) that protect drinking water and water quality. It sits on top of the 2020 measure (0.15 mill, $50M cap, passed with about 71%). A no vote ends the program per the county natural-resources director; land already protected stays protected.

who_funds_yes.text: Political committee 'Protect Water, Preserve Land': $45,050 monetary + $8,926 in-kind per the Supervisor of Elections; donors Florida Wildlife Corridor Foundation $22,500, Trust for Public Land about $15,800, NCDG Management LLC (Sarasota; business not named in the filing) $10,000, and individuals; spending went mainly to Simmer House (Fort Myers) for marketing.

who_funds_no.text: No organized opposition committee found; opposition is individual voters (e.g. Trent Wayman) citing cost of living and distrust of county handling of funds.

races.title: City of Holmes Beach Referendum: vacating a 10-foot alleyway at 2902 Avenue East

m.name: City of Holmes Beach Referendum: vacating a 10-foot alleyway at 2902 Avenue East
m.summary: Ballot asks whether the City should vacate an unused, inaccessible 10-foot-wide alleyway bisecting the beachfront property at 2902 Avenue E in favor of that property's owner. Yes = vacate, No = deny. A Holmes Beach charter provision requires voter approval for vacations of this kind. The article reports the alley is about 150 feet long and no payment to the city was reported.
m.who_funds_yes: Not found (no campaign committee reported in sources reviewed). The property owner, Blowfish Island Inc. (managed by Benjamin ten Haff), is the beneficiary and is represented by attorney Garret Barnes.
supporters: Property owner Blowfish Island Inc. via attorney Garret Barnes (bought the lot in 2024 for $7.25 million and plans two homes instead of three)
City Attorney Randy Mora called it a housekeeping action
Holmes Beach commission voted 4-0 on June 23, 2026 (Dan Diggins absent) to adopt Resolution 26-06 placing it on the ballot; the supporting ordinance passed unanimously at two hearings in 2025
opponents: Resident Nancy Deal, the only public commenter, questioned giving up public land; Commissioner Jessica Patel asked whether the city was getting paid. No organized opposition reported in sources reviewed.
m.gaps: Who funds yes/no not found. Charter basis (supermajority + referendum requirement) not confirmed for this specific alley. An Islander correction states the alley is NOT a beach access path and runs north-south between six privately owned plats; the Sun article reports no payment to the city.

races.title: Parrish Fire District Referendum: Authorization to Increase Annual Special Assessments for Fire Protection Services

m.name: Parrish Fire District Referendum: Authorization to Increase Annual Special Assessments for Fire Protection Services
m.summary: Ballot asks "Shall the Parrish Fire District be authorized to increase its base rate of assessment" by an additional flat $68.00 per developed residential, commercial and industrial parcel per year (vacant, acreage and golf course parcels excluded). Stated purpose: fund additional personnel to move the standard firefighter schedule from 56 to 42 hours per week, consistent with Florida Statutes s. 633.508(7)(c). The assessment is a flat per-parcel charge, not a percentage of property value. Fire Chief Stacey Bailey said shorter schedules support firefighters' mental health and that Florida law encourages the 42-hour policy. Expected total revenue and number of firefighters to be added were not stated in the sources reviewed. Background: the district's 5-year plan says a 2020 referendum to raise the assessment by $80 was approved by voters.
m.who_funds_yes: Not found (no campaign committee reported in sources reviewed).
supporters: Fire Chief Stacey Bailey (district chief) is quoted supporting the schedule change
opponents: None identified in the sources reviewed (no organized opposition found; not verified that none exists)
m.gaps: Total revenue, firefighters to be added, and any organized opposition not found. One district Nextdoor post claims an earlier assessment referendum was not approved, conflicting with the 5-year plan's statement that the 2020 $80 measure passed; unresolved.
